name: Gastrointestinal Tract Arteriovenous Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiologic Diagnostic Criteria for Gastrointestinal AVM

criteria.description: Recurrent or chronic gastrointestinal bleeding without other identifiable cause
Visualization of arteriovenous malformation on angiography, CT angiogram, or MRI
Endoscopic identification of tortuous, dilated vessels consistent with AVM
Histopathological confirmation of abnormal direct arterial to venous connections without intervening capillaries

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding plus imaging confirmation of AVM
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is rarely required but can confirm diagnosis; endoscopic findings support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Often manifests as melena or hematochezia
searchTerms: ongoing blood loss in digestive tract

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible arteriovenous malformations on angiographic imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Direct visualization of abnormal vascular connections
searchTerms: visible abnormal blood vessels on imaging

common.symptomName: Iron deficiency anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
searchTerms: iron deficiency anemia due to bleeding
low iron anemia from gut bleeding

common.notes: Detected by fecal occult blood testing
searchTerms: hidden blood loss in digestive tract

common.notes: Non-specific symptom related to lesion location
Tortuous, dilated vessels seen in affected segments

occasional.notes: May occur in severe bleeding episodes

searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells
palpitations caused by low blood count

occasional.notes: May be related to lesion location and size

rare.symptomName: Intestinal ischemia secondary to vascular steal phenomenon
rare.notes: Rare complication due to altered blood flow
searchTerms: gut tissue damage from poor blood supply

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure due to large AVMs
searchTerms: heart failure from high blood flow
high-output cardiac failure due to AVMs

laboratory: Iron deficiency anemia on complete blood count
imaging: CT angiography or MRI showing abnormal vascular connections
other: Endoscopic identification of dilated, tortuous vessels
Histopathology showing direct arterial to venous connections without capillaries

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of capillary or cavernous vascular lesions rather than direct AV connections
Family history and genetic testing positive for HHT mutations

redFlags: Massive gastrointestinal hemorrhage causing hemodynamic instability
Refractory iron deficiency anemia despite supplementation
Signs of high-output cardiac failure in the context of large AVMs
references: Gastrointestinal arteriovenous malformations: clinical features and management. Gastroenterology Clinics. 2022.
